title: Long JPM — Q2 Earnings Beat + NIM Expansion + $50B Buyback Authorization
entry: $336–345. Prioritize entries below $340 on intraday CPI-day weakness; post-8:30 AM clarity provides a cleaner setup as the earnings-driven re-rating overlaps with macro stabilization. Avoid chasing above $345 before NIM expansion commentary is confirmed on the earnings call.
stop_loss: $318 daily close (~6.5% below $340 midpoint) — a close at $318 implies one of: (1) NIM guidance on the Q2 earnings call was negative (net interest income declining vs Q1, contradicting the rate-environment thesis); (2) CPI prints ≥3.9% and Warsh signals a live July 28 meeting, compressing financial-sector multiples by repricing the cost of capital at JPM's refinancing facilities; or (3) credit quality metrics exceed expectations negatively (loan-loss provisions rising sharply, indicating early-cycle credit deterioration not flagged in guidance).
targets: $362 — NIM expansion confirmed on the Q2 earnings call (net interest income above Q1 on portfolio-weighted basis); JPM Q3 guidance beats Q2 consensus by 5%+; $50B buyback commences at a pace removing ~1.5% of shares outstanding in 60 days; +6.4% from $340 entry; cover 40% of position

$378 — Bank earnings season completes with all four large reporters (BAC, GS, WFC, C) showing broad NIM expansion and sub-3% charge-off rates; sector rotation out of tech into financials accelerates as CPI muddle-through (~3.8%) keeps rates elevated, benefiting NIM; +11.2%; cover 40%

$395 — Full re-rating: August PCE confirms disinflation trajectory (core below 3.0%) while rates stay elevated through September; JPM operates in the optimal environment (wide spreads without recessionary credit deterioration); buyback pace accelerates; sell-side raises PTs to $400+; +16.1%; hold final 20%
catalyst: Q2 2026 EPS $6.14 vs $5.59 consensus (+9.84% beat); revenue $58.02B vs $51.09B consensus; $50B buyback authorized — largest in JPM history; quarterly dividend raised to $1.65/share. BAC also beat (EPS $1.21 vs $1.11, revenue +14.2% YoY) and GS massively beat (EPS $20.98 vs $14.54, ROTE 23.5%) — broad bank earnings season opening constructively creates sector tailwind for JPM multiple expansion.
thesis:
JPM reported Q2 2026 EPS of $6.14 vs $5.59 consensus (+9.84% beat) this morning with revenue of $58.02B vs $51.09B consensus. The board simultaneously authorized a $50B buyback and raised the quarterly dividend to $1.65/share. Capital return signals of this magnitude are only sustainable if management has high conviction in forward earnings quality, suggesting NIM expansion is not a one-quarter phenomenon.

The rate environment is structurally supportive for JPM's NIM. With 10Y at 4.62% and 30Y above 5.00% for the second consecutive session, the spread between JPM's deposit cost (anchored to Fed funds) and its lending rate (indexed to SOFR + Treasury yields) is near cycle highs. The BofA three-hike scenario — if it materializes — would extend NIM expansion into 2027, providing a durable earnings floor the market is not yet pricing into the multiple.

The broader bank earnings context reinforces the thesis. BAC beat (EPS $1.21 vs $1.11, revenue +14.2% YoY) and GS crushed consensus (EPS $20.98 vs $14.54, ROTE 23.5%) — a coherent message that higher rates have been net positive for financial sector ROE. Sector rotation dynamics favor this: institutional investors underweight in financials relative to tech are being presented with a catalyst to rebalance. QQQ is down 2.15% today while JPM is up 0.78% — that divergence is the embryo of a rotation trade.

The $50B buyback reduces share supply at a pace that mechanically supports the price even if the macro environment deteriorates modestly. At $340, JPM trades at approximately 13.5x forward earnings — below the historical 14–15x fair value for a well-capitalized money-center bank in a NIM expansion cycle. Reversion to 14.5x forward (approximately $365–370) is the base case without any incremental macro improvement.
bull_case: CPI ≤3.5% today triggers a BUY upgrade, rate-cut expectations price in a soft landing, NIM expansion sustains into 2027, and JPM's buyback creates a floor that allows multiple expansion to 15–16x forward. Target3 at $395 achieved within 4–5 weeks if the September hike probability collapses and bank re-rating continues.
bear_case: NIM guidance disappoints — management signals Q3 NIM compression as deposit rates finally re-price higher relative to loan spreads. OR CPI ≥3.9% triggers September hike expectations that compress financial-sector multiples as market prices in recessionary credit quality deterioration. OR loan-loss provisions for Q3 are guided materially higher than Q2 actuals, indicating early-cycle deterioration in the commercial real estate or consumer credit book.
invalidation: $318 daily close; OR NIM guidance on the Q2 earnings call explicitly signals net interest income decline vs Q1 2026; OR September FOMC hike probability rises above 80% (financial sector multiples compress as recession risk premia spike); OR JPM announces material credit quality deterioration in commercial real estate (CRE charge-off rate above 2.0% on the Q3 call).
